about: Authored quick-round questions only. Difficulty is an editorial estimate, not measured accuracy. IDs and answer meanings are immutable once deployed: retire a flawed ID and add a new one. Ranked schedules and the full assessment use their existing banks.

items.prompt: Mercury is closest to the Sun. Which planet has the hotter surface?
items.explanation: Venus wins: its thick atmosphere traps heat. Being closer to the Sun is not enough to make Mercury hotter.

items.prompt: An ice cube floats in water. What makes that possible?
options: Ice is less dense than liquid water
Ice is denser than liquid water
items.explanation: Water expands as it freezes, so the same mass takes up more space. That lower density lets ordinary ice float.

items.prompt: A sound has to travel one kilometre. Where does it arrive sooner?
items.explanation: Sound travels about 1,500 m/s in seawater versus roughly 340 m/s in air. Water carries the vibration much faster.

items.prompt: What makes the Moon look like a crescent on an ordinary night?
options: We see only part of its sunlit half
Earth's shadow covers most of it
items.explanation: The Moon's phases come from our changing view of its sunlit half. Earth's shadow causes a lunar eclipse, not the monthly phases.

items.prompt: Two solid cubes are the same size: one gold, one lead. Which weighs more?
items.explanation: Gold is denser: about 19.3 g/cm³ versus 11.3 for lead. Lead feels heavy until you give gold the same volume.

items.prompt: Which visible light has the longer wavelength?
items.explanation: Red sits at the long-wavelength end of visible light; blue sits nearer the short-wavelength end. Bluer does not mean longer.

items.prompt: How many hearts does an octopus have?
items.explanation: Two hearts send blood to the gills. A third sends it around the body. Eight arms, three hearts.

items.prompt: Which living animal is more closely related to a whale?
items.explanation: Hippos are whales' closest living relatives. A shared swimming lifestyle makes seals look like the better guess.

items.prompt: Whose typical body cell has more chromosomes?
items.explanation: Chimpanzees have 48; humans have 46. Human chromosome 2 formed from the fusion of two ancestral chromosomes.

items.prompt: In 'small intestine' and 'large intestine', what does 'large' mainly describe?
items.explanation: The large intestine is wider. The small intestine is actually the longer one, despite its name.

items.prompt: A bat uses echolocation. Does that mean it cannot see?
items.explanation: Bats have working eyes. Echolocation adds information about their surroundings; it does not replace vision because they are blind.

items.prompt: Under all that pale fur, what colour is a polar bear's skin?
items.explanation: The skin is black. The pale appearance comes from the fur, so the colour you see is not the colour underneath.

items.prompt: Why is it summer in Australia when it is winter in Europe?
options: Earth's distance from the Sun changes
items.explanation: The hemispheres tilt toward the Sun at opposite times of year. A change in Earth's distance would affect both hemispheres together.

items.prompt: Which ocean covers more area?
items.explanation: The Pacific is the largest ocean basin. NOAA notes that all the continents could fit inside it.

items.prompt: Much of Antarctica is a desert. What qualifies it?
items.explanation: Deserts are defined by dryness, not heat. Antarctica's interior receives very little snowfall despite all the ice already there.

items.prompt: You stand at the North Pole in June. On a clear day, does the Sun set?
options: No, it stays above the horizon
items.explanation: The North Pole tilts toward the Sun during northern summer. Earth keeps spinning, but the pole stays on the sunlit side.

items.prompt: Which summit is farther from the centre of Earth?
items.explanation: Everest is higher above sea level. Chimborazo is nearer the equator, where Earth's bulge puts its summit farther from the centre.

items.prompt: Put Everest in the ocean with its base at Challenger Deep. Would its summit reach the surface?
options: No, it would still be underwater
items.explanation: Challenger Deep is roughly 11 km below the surface; Everest rises about 8.85 km above sea level. There would still be about 2 km of water overhead.

items.prompt: Before Mario, what did Nintendo originally make?
items.explanation: Nintendo began making hanafuda playing cards in Kyoto in 1889. Video games came much later.

items.prompt: Before streaming, which format did Netflix rent by mail?
items.explanation: Netflix launched its online DVD rental store in 1998. The red envelope came before the streaming queue.

items.prompt: LEGO started making toys in 1932. What were those early toys mainly made of?
items.explanation: Ole Kirk Kristiansen's early toys were wooden, including cars and aeroplanes. The plastic brick was a later chapter.

items.prompt: Where was Tetris created?
items.explanation: Alexey Pajitnov created Tetris in Moscow in 1984 on an Electronika 60 computer. Its later Nintendo success can make Tokyo feel like the obvious answer.

items.prompt: The Oscar statuette design introduced in 2016 is made from what?
items.explanation: The Academy returned to a cast-bronze statuette finished in 24-karat gold. The gold is the finish, not the whole statue.

items.prompt: Your queen is still on the chessboard. Can you promote a pawn to a second queen?
items.explanation: Promotion is not limited to pieces that have been captured. A pawn reaching the last rank can become another queen.

items.prompt: Bubble Wrap began as an attempt to make what?
items.explanation: The inventors first tried to sell it as textured wallpaper. Protecting packages turned out to be the better use.

items.prompt: QR codes were originally developed for which setting?
items.explanation: DENSO WAVE released the QR code in 1994. The auto industry used it to track production and logistics long before phone menus.

items.prompt: What inspired the hooks in VELCRO fasteners?
options: Burrs caught in fur and fabric
items.explanation: George de Mestral examined clinging burrs and found tiny hooks. He copied that hook-and-loop mechanism into a reusable fastener.

items.prompt: What is the dark writing material in an ordinary 'lead' pencil?
items.explanation: The core uses graphite, usually mixed with clay. The everyday name 'pencil lead' does not describe the metal lead.

items.prompt: A thick potato is in a microwave. Is it cooked from the inside out?
options: No, heat also has to conduct inward
items.explanation: Microwaves penetrate only so far into thick food. The outer layers absorb energy, and heat conducts toward the centre.

items.prompt: Botanically, the potato you eat is a swollen what?
items.explanation: A potato is a stem tuber. Its 'eyes' are buds that can grow new shoots, a clue to what it really is.

items.prompt: A fair coin lands heads five times in independent flips. Chance of tails next?
items.explanation: The coin has no memory. With independent fair flips, the next result is still 50–50; tails is not 'due'.

items.prompt: A $100 price rises 20%, then falls 20%. Where does it end?
items.explanation: $100 × 1.20 = $120, then $120 × 0.80 = $96. The second percentage applies to a different starting amount.

items.prompt: For 23 independent, uniformly distributed birthdays on 365 days, is the chance of a shared birthday above 50%?
items.explanation: It is about 50.7%. There are 253 pairs of people, so there are many more chances for a match than 23 might suggest.

items.prompt: You drive 60 miles at 30 mph, then 60 miles at 60 mph. Average speed for the whole trip?
items.explanation: The trip takes 2 hours plus 1 hour. That's 120 miles in 3 hours: 40 mph. You spend more time at the slower speed.

items.prompt: Roll two independent fair six-sided dice. Which total is more likely?
items.explanation: Six ordered outcomes make 7; only (6, 6) makes 12. That is 6 chances in 36 versus 1 in 36.

items.prompt: A bat and ball cost $1.10 together. The bat costs $1 more than the ball. Ball's price?
items.explanation: At 5 cents for the ball, the bat is $1.05 and the total is $1.10. A 10-cent ball would make the total $1.20.

items.prompt: AlphaGo's famous match against Lee Sedol was played in which game?
items.explanation: Lee Sedol faced AlphaGo at Go in 2016. AlphaZero later tackled chess, shogi and Go.

items.prompt: Why did OpenAI initially withhold the full GPT-2 model in 2019?
options: It could not generate text yet
items.explanation: OpenAI released a smaller model first while studying misuse risks. The full 1.5-billion-parameter model came later that year.

items.prompt: In a language model, is one token always one whole word?
options: No, it can be part of a word
Yes, one word always equals one token
items.explanation: Tokens can be word pieces, whole words, punctuation or characters. A word count is not a reliable token count.

items.prompt: ImageNet was built around which kind of data?
items.explanation: ImageNet organises images into a hierarchy of concepts. Its image-recognition challenge helped make deep learning famous.

items.prompt: What powered the original 1966 ELIZA chatbot?
options: Rules that matched and rearranged text
items.explanation: ELIZA used keyword rules and response templates. Convincing conversation existed long before today's large language models.

items.prompt: The original Transformer replaced recurrence with what main mechanism?
items.explanation: The 2017 paper built the Transformer around attention, removing recurrent and convolutional layers from that architecture.

items.prompt: A classifier assigns 90% confidence. Does that number alone prove it is right 90% of the time?
items.explanation: A score is not a guarantee of calibration. A model can be confident more often than it is correct, just like a player here.

items.prompt: For the same number of weights, which needs less raw storage, ignoring overhead?
items.explanation: Four bits per weight is one quarter of sixteen. Real memory use also includes scales, activations and other overhead.

items.prompt: A RAG assistant needs today's policy document. What is the retrieval step for?
options: Finding relevant text to supply to the model
items.explanation: Retrieval supplies outside information for generation. Fetching a document is different from updating the model's learned weights.

items.prompt: During BERT's masked-word pretraining, which context can help fill a blank?
items.explanation: BERT was designed to learn from left and right context together. The 'B' stands for bidirectional.

items.prompt: How did AlphaZero learn game strategy, given the rules?
options: A database of human expert games
items.explanation: AlphaZero trained by playing against itself. Unlike the original AlphaGo, it did not need human game records to learn its strategy.

items.prompt: Which was published first?
items.explanation: The Transformer paper appeared in 2017; GPT-3's paper appeared in 2020. GPT-3 built on the Transformer family.

items.prompt: The largest model in the original GPT-3 paper had how many parameters?
items.explanation: The paper's largest GPT-3 model had 175 billion parameters. The decimal point changes the answer by a factor of ten.

items.prompt: In a standard denoising diffusion model, how is a new image generated?
options: By retrieving an unchanged training image
items.explanation: The model learns a reverse process that turns noise into an image step by step. It is not simply an image-search engine.

items.prompt: In neural-network training, what does 'dropout' mean?
items.explanation: Dropout randomly omits units during training to reduce overfitting. It is not the same operation as permanently pruning a network.

items.prompt: GPT-3 gets a few worked examples in its prompt, with no training step. What changes?
items.explanation: The original few-shot setup supplied examples as text, with no gradient updates. The model used a new context, not newly trained weights.

items.prompt: Only 1% of emails are spam. A filter labels every email 'not spam'. Its accuracy?
items.explanation: It gets the 99% non-spam messages right while catching zero spam. High accuracy can hide complete failure on the class you care about.

items.prompt: A filter flags 100 emails as spam; 20 really are spam. Its precision?
items.explanation: Precision asks how many positive predictions were correct: 20 divided by 100. It is not the fraction of all spam caught.

items.prompt: Did the original GPT-4 technical report disclose its parameter count?
items.explanation: The report withheld model-size and architecture details. A widely repeated parameter count is not the same as a number disclosed in that report.

items.prompt: What task was the original Transformer paper mainly evaluated on?
items.explanation: Its main experiments translated English to German and French. Chatbots were not the original paper's benchmark.

items.prompt: For a two-token output: P(A)=0.6, P(B)=0.4; best continuations have P(x|A)=0.5, P(y|B)=0.9. Which sequence is likelier?
items.explanation: P(Ax)=0.6×0.5=0.30; P(By)=0.4×0.9=0.36. Taking the most likely first token need not give the most likely whole sequence.

items.prompt: In top-p (nucleus) sampling, does p set a fixed number of candidate tokens?
items.explanation: The nucleus grows or shrinks with the probability distribution. Top-k fixes a token count; top-p uses cumulative probability.

items.prompt: A perfectly calibrated model makes many 70%-confidence predictions. Roughly how many should be right?
items.explanation: Calibration means the confidence matches the long-run success rate. Being well calibrated still allows mistakes.

items.prompt: In the original LoRA method, what gets trained?
items.explanation: LoRA freezes the pretrained weights and trains low-rank updates. Adapting a model does not always mean updating every original weight.
